producing_agent.identity: Cursor Grok 4.6 (cloud agent, under J. Brown direction)

hypothesis: On the truncated variable-x EML language (k≤5, π(t)∝4^{-|t|}), Gibbs access P(z)=Φ_z/Z is not a function of shortest depth. Same-min-size finite fibers can differ in mass by a factor of at least 2 because of min-shell multiplicity. Extra shells and master-formula gradient recovery are not claimed.
decision: Accept the EML-native Gibbs-vs-shortest split if and only if the registered k=3 finite class has Φ_max/Φ_min ≥ 2 and the zero identity holds. Do not promote gradient recovery. Do not claim the Sq extra-shell mechanism transferred.

audit_card.target_object: Numerical fibers of the leaf-labeled EML grammar S → 1 | x | eml(S,S) through 5 internal nodes, under the Gibbs prior π(t)∝4^{-|t|}.
audit_card.decision: Accept or reject: same-min-size Gibbs mass split on the truncated language; gradient recovery remains untested; extra-shell transfer from the monomial toy is not claimed.
audit_card.representation: Enumerated VarTree census; 10-decimal quantization of the 6-point positive grid for fiber ids; exact real eval for the zero identity.
audit_card.data_clock: None. Closed finite language fragment. Φ and Z are exact finite sums, not samples.
material_assumptions: The language and grid are those of experiments/eml_variable_spectrum.
Gibbs base 4 is a modelling choice inherited from the monomial toy, not a canonical temperature.
Rounded grid tuples cluster functions; only the zero identity is treated as algebraic.
Shortest-only Q assigns one min-shell unit per fiber; P sums every inhabitant.

objects.Tree: full binary EML trees; leaves in {1,x}
objects.Fiber: level set of the 10-decimal 6-point grid tuple
objects.Phi: sum_t 4^{-(2 k(t)+1)} over trees in the fiber

mathematical_claim.types_domains_units: Masses are dimensionless probabilities after dividing by the language partition function Z. Support is the finite k≤5 fragment.
mathematical_claim.exact_claim: There exist two fully-finite fibers with min_internal=3 whose Φ ratio is at least 2. eml(a,eml(eml(a,1),1))=0 for a in {1,x} on the registered grid. Shortest depth does not determine Φ. Gradient recovery is not a claim.
mathematical_claim.quantifiers: Existential for the k=3 split and the zero identity. Universal for labeled Catalan counts on k=0..5.
mathematical_claim.assumptions: Real eml; overflow/domain failures are undefined and excluded from the finite-fiber split; Gibbs base 4.
mathematical_claim.identification_conditions: The zero witness uses exact eval, not rounded fiber ids. The split uses finite (no-undef) fibers only.
mathematical_claim.derivation_dependencies: Odrzywołek arXiv:2603.21852 for eml. The variable-x enumerator for the language. No 1-D invariant is assumed.
mathematical_claim.coordinate_invariance: Pretty-print is a gauge. The grid is a registered representation. The zero identity is algebraic in a.
mathematical_claim.edge_limiting_null_cases: If every k=3 finite fiber were a singleton, the split would die. Extra shells at k=5 are recorded and are not the claimed mechanism.

compute.sampling: exhaustive leaf-labeled trees with k<=5 internal nodes. Exact Φ/Z. No Monte Carlo.

claim_boundary: Accepted only as: on this truncated language, Gibbs mass is not a function of shortest depth, and the zero function has two size-3 formulas. Not gradient recovery. Not the Sq extra-shell transfer. Not function identity from the grid except the exact zero identity.
